chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm,

He said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Which of the two is superior: staying in Mecca or staying in Medina?' He said, 'What do you say?' I said, 'And what is my saying in comparison to your saying?' He said, 'Indeed, your saying is referred back to my saying.' I said to him, 'As for me, I believe that staying in Medina is superior to staying in Mecca.'

He said, 'If you say that, then indeed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said that - on the Day of Fitr (Eid al-Fitr), when he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and greeted him in the mosque, then he said, "We have been favored today over the people by our greeting upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)."'
ai.seo_question: Which city is considered superior for staying: Mecca or Medina, according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Rida (AS) validates the superiority of residing in Medina over Mecca, linking it to the specific virtue of greeting the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the Masjid on Eid al-Fitr. The Imam’s confirmation relies on a precedent set by Imam Al-Sadiq (AS), who emphasized that the believers' salutations upon the Prophet hold a distinct merit, thereby elevating the spiritual status of Medina as the primary locus of this interaction. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unique sanctity of the Prophet's resting place and the ritual significance of Eid greetings within the sacred precincts of Medina.
